model: One day I'd really like to set up a business offering healthy lunch boxes for office workers. The idea came from my own experience. I work in a big office building in Hanoi, and there are hundreds of people there who are too busy to cook. Most of them just order fried rice or noodles every day, which leads to people feeling tired and putting on weight. I think there's a gap in the market for affordable meals that are actually healthy. My target customers would be young professionals like me, who care about their health but don't have much time. The plan would be simple: customers order the day before through a small app, and we deliver the food to their building at noon. Because we'd cook a fixed number of meals, there'd be very little waste, which means that we could keep prices low. The start-up costs wouldn't be huge either, mainly a kitchen, a couple of cooks and some delivery staff. I'd rely on word of mouth at first, because if people in one office like it, they'll tell their colleagues. Of course, it's risky. Many food businesses close within two years due to high rent and competition, and I'd probably need at least a year just to break even. But the idea of being my own boss really appeals to me. Maybe in a few years, when I've saved enough, I'll finally take the plunge.
